thread:
tori: Heads up — we got a noisy alert from the policy scanner. After yesterday's workspace-affinity rollout, some service accounts can see projects in other orgs. :eyes:
ops-bot: policy-scan: HIGH severity: scope_expansion detected for svc-account:inference-router. Affected resources: 12 projects across 3 orgs. See /alerts/2015004321
sam: WTF. Is this the mapping change in project-router v2? I thought we pinned workspace affinity to org_id + region.
tori: yes that was the change. The migration script changed the default fallback to `workspace_id` instead of `org_id` when a project lacked explicit binding.
eli: do we have a quick repro? I can run an authz query against the new mapping service.
rachel: added logs from the deploy: `mapping-service v2` migrated ~2600 entries at 02:11 UTC. Patch diff attached in PR #412 (link: https://github.com/redwood/mapping-service/pull/412)
tori: sample ACL that caused expansion: ```json
{"project_id":"p-987","bindings":[{"role":"reader","principal":"svc:inference-router"}],"workspace_affinity":null}```
ops-bot: config-check: migration default fallback = `workspace_affinity: derived_from_request` (was `derived_from_org`).
sam: so if workspace_affinity==null, we now infer from the incoming request workspace which may be from a different org -> grants access. That's the hole.
eli: I'm running a scoped query now: `SELECT binding FROM authz WHERE principal='svc:inference-router' AND project_id='p-987'` -> returns binding with workspace_affinity set to `w-123 (org-b)` but project belongs to `org-a`.
tori: mitigation plan: 1) flip the feature-flag for mapping-service v2 to off (prevent further writes), 2) roll back migration for entries where `workspace_affinity` != project's org, 3) revoke temporary tokens for svc:inference-router, 4) collect audit log + list of impacted orgs to notify. Who can flip the flag?
sam: I can flip the flag now. Doing: `deployctl cfg set mapping-service.default-fallback=org-derived --env prod`
sam: done — flag flipped at 2015004500 UTC. :white_check_mark:
tori: nice. Eli/rachel, can you generate the list of impacted projects and orgs so we can notify legal/compliance? We need KMS access review too — if any cross-org kms unwraps happened.
eli: running queries on audit-writer for decrypt events: `service=kms AND principal=svc:inference-router AND time>2024-09-18T02:00:00Z` -> no decrypt entries so far, only list/get. Will post CSV in 10m.
rachel: started rollback job: `migration-revert --filter 'workspace_affinity!=org' --dry-run` -> shows 18 projects to be reverted. Planning to run in 5 to restore explicit org-derived affinity.
tori: please create an incident page and assign Sev2. Include timeline and PRs. Also rotate any long-lived keys for service accounts that had broad access — we should assume potential exposure until proven otherwise.
sam: incident created: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2024-2987. Owner: sam.
ops-bot: audit-log: policy-change recorded by sam at 2015004500 UTC.
eli: rollback executed at 2015005100 UTC. Reverted 18 records, verified via `authz verify` script. No further expansion queries return cross-org bindings.
rachel: confirm no KMS decrypts by that principal between migration time and rollback. Verified.
tori: action items: 1) postmortem, 2) add unit tests for fallback logic, 3) make mapping migration idempotent with explicit `org_id` requirement, 4) add alert to policy-scan for inferred-affinity changes.
sam: I'll open the hotfix PR to require `org_id` in migration and add gating test. PR #415.
eli: will run a full scan across all service-accounts tonight and drop a report in the incident doc.
ops-bot: followup-reminder set for 72h.
tori: thanks team. Keep updates in the incident page. Notify customers that reported suspicious access once we have full scope. :pray:
